source.title: Superposition Without Compression: Why Entangled Representations Are the Default

record.file_problem: The supplied post gives no details of the toy example and links to an external Google Drive note that is not included.
record.tranche_reason: It argues that superposition may occur even with sufficient capacity, so polysemanticity alone should not be treated as proof of underparameterization. The supplied text does not establish that the toy example measures neuron polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The post states a qualitative conclusion about a toy example but gives no architecture, procedure, or quantitative results. Its stated result concerns superposition and solution-space prevalence, not a measurement of individual neurons' polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The post argues that superposition may be the default even with sufficient capacity. This bears on V3, which treats capacity as the cause, and on V4. But the supplied text reports no architecture, procedure or numbers. The toy example is only in an external note that was not supplied. The argument also concerns superposition rather than measured neuron polysemanticity, a conflation a commenter points out. So no verdict can rest on results in the text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The author cautions against inferring underparameterization from polysemanticity, and argues superposition may be the default even with sufficient capacity because disentangled solutions are rare among low-loss solutions. He frames this as rough speculation.
record.recipe_differences: A qualitative toy-example argument about solution-space prevalence; it does not describe the neuron-analysis or activation-function methods of the original sources.

fits_no_version.finding: The author asserts that a toy example shows disentangled solutions are a tiny fraction of low-loss solutions even with sufficient capacity. No details or numbers are given in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition (entangled representations) is prevalent in the low-loss solution space even when capacity is sufficient.
